title: Timeout Patterns
description: Learn to implement timeout patterns to prevent slow services from degrading your system.

data.text: Timeouts are the simplest and most important resilience pattern. Amazon, Netflix, and Google all enforce strict timeouts on all outbound calls. A slow downstream service can quickly exhaust thread pools and cause cascading failures without timeouts.

Without timeouts, a slow or hanging downstream service can block threads indefinitely. In a thread-pool-based system, this quickly exhausts available threads, causing requests to queue and eventually time out at the client. The failure cascades up the call chain.

data.title: Timeout Categories
items: Connection timeout: Time to establish a connection
Request timeout: Time to receive the first byte of response
Total timeout: Maximum time for the entire operation
Idle timeout: Time to close idle connections in the pool

data.title: Timeout Cascade
data.text: Always set timeouts on all outbound calls. A missing timeout on one call can block a thread, causing timeouts upstream. Set reasonable defaults: 2-5 seconds for HTTP, 30-60 seconds for long-running operations.

items.question: What timeout values should I use?
items.answer: Use p99 latency + buffer as your timeout. If 99% of calls complete in 500ms, set timeout to 2-3 seconds. This accommodates normal variance while failing fast on problems.

items.question: Should timeout be higher at the gateway or inside services?
items.answer: Gateway timeout should be higher than internal service timeouts. If internal services have 3s timeouts, set gateway timeout to 5-10s to allow for retries.

items.question: What about gRPC deadlines?
items.answer: gRPC supports deadlines natively. Set a deadline on all gRPC calls; the server cancels the operation if the deadline passes.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Always set timeouts on all outbound calls
Use connection, request, and total timeouts appropriately
Base timeout values on p99 latency + buffer
Timeouts prevent cascading failures from slow services
data.takeaway: Timeouts are the simplest and most effective resilience pattern; never skip them.
